files.purpose: MCPKeyPanel.swift defines the singleton floating panel (MCPKeyPanel.shared) that a user pastes an MCP server's key or other field values into. present(entry:model:) (:12-20) opens the catalog entry's keysURL in the default browser with NSWorkspace, builds an MCPKeyPanelView with .presentedChrome() and the AppModel environment, and hands it to present(_:), which is inherited from the new FloatingGuidePanel base created with width 380 (:10). MCPKeyPanelView (:24-195) renders the header (MCPIcon, the entry name, the word "Connect", an xmark close button), three numbered steps for an entry with a key page or two without one, one secure or plain monospaced field per MCPField with a folder picker for path fields (folders only for the entry id "filesystem"), and a "Save and connect" / "Sign in" button. That button commits through model.mcp.connect and closes the panel at once, and the panel also closes itself when the entry becomes connected.

private func stepRow(_ number: Int, text: Text, accessory: AnyView? = nil) -> some View (:107-124)
@ViewBuilder private func fieldView(_ field: MCPField) -> some View (:126-168)

state_owned: MCPKeyPanel.shared, the process-wide singleton (:8); at B3 it owns no stored properties of its own - the NSPanel (private(set) var panel) and the escape monitor token (private var escapeMonitor) and the width (380) are stored in the FloatingGuidePanel base
MCPKeyPanelView's @FocusState focusedField: String? - set to the first field's key on appear (:59) and bound per field with .focused($focusedField, equals: field.key) (:144)
Field text is not owned here: draftBinding reads MCPStore.value(for:of:) and writes MCPStore.setDraft (:170-175)
side_effects: Every present opens entry.keysURL in the default browser when it parses as a URL (:13-15); there is no re-entry guard, so a second present reopens the page and rebuilds the view (upstream defect 69, PR-MCP-214 - unchanged at B3)

present(content) (:19) creates or reuses one floating non-activating NSPanel, sizes it to the content measured at 380 wide with a 100 floor, places it at the main screen's visible top right inset 24, installs the Escape key-down monitor and orders it front (all in FloatingGuidePanel.swift:16-26)
The "Open it again" link reopens the key page in the browser (:94)
The path picker runs a modal NSOpenPanel and writes the chosen url.path as a draft (:177-189)
save() calls model.mcp.connect(entry), which commits drafts and starts a probe, then closes the panel without waiting (:191-194)
The panel closes itself when model.mcp.state(for: entry.id).isConnected becomes true (:61-63)
platform_assumptions: AppKit NSWorkspace.shared.open for the key page (:14)
AppKit NSOpenPanel with canChooseDirectories/canChooseFiles switched on entry.id == "filesystem" (:178-186)

The NSPanel mechanics (.nonactivatingPanel style mask, .floating level, canJoinAllSpaces/fullScreenAuxiliary, hidden window buttons, NSEvent local monitor on keyCode 53) are no longer in this file; at B3 they live in FloatingGuidePanel.swift:33-70

feature_notes: B2->B3, single commit d70cff8fe ("refactor: audit cleanups - five bug fixes, shared MCP and provider code, layer rules restored"): MCPKeyPanel changed from a standalone final class to `final class MCPKeyPanel: FloatingGuidePanel` (:7). The B2 stored properties `private var panel: NSPanel?` and `private var escapeMonitor: Any?` (B2 :10-11), the inline measure/size/place/monitor/order-front block in present (B2 :22-30), close() (B2 :33-36), makePanel() (B2 :38-61), startEscapeMonitor() (B2 :63-70) and stopEscapeMonitor() (B2 :72-75) were deleted and replaced by `private init() { super.init(width: 380) }` (:10) and `present(content)` (:19).

SOURCE FACT: the moved code is the same. FloatingGuidePanel.swift:16-70 (read in full for this comparison) matches the deleted B2 block with only the literal 380 swapped for the stored width: the same fittingSize measurement rounded up, the 100 floor, origin visible.maxX - width - 24 / visible.maxY - height - 24, the style mask [.nonactivatingPanel, .fullSizeContentView, .titled, .closable], the same panel properties, the three hidden window buttons, and the same keyCode 53 local monitor installed once and removed in close(). The key panel does not override close(), so the escape monitor's self.close() and the view's onDone ({ [weak self] in self?.close() }, :16) reach the base close(), as the B2 close() did. No observable behaviour of the key panel changed.

The unused `@Environment(AppModel.self) private var envModel` (B2 :84) was removed from MCPKeyPanelView. The view already used its stored `model` everywhere and still gets `.environment(model)` (:18), so nothing observable changed.

Everything from MCPKeyPanelView's body onward (the steps, strings, fonts, fields, pickPath filesystem rule, draftBinding, save, onSubmit, the isConnected auto-close and the first-field focus) is unchanged byte for byte. Lines shifted: B2 1-9 = B3 1-9; B2 15-21 = B3 12-18; B2 79-83 = B3 24-28 (-55); B2 85-251 = B3 29-195 (-56).

Why it matters: every spec record for this file cites B2 line numbers and must be re-cited. The records whose evidence was the window mechanics (PR-MCP-214's close(), PR-MCP-215, PR-MCP-216, UI-MCP-070 and its note citing :41 .nonactivatingPanel) must now cite FloatingGuidePanel.swift (present :16-26, close :28-31, makePanel :33-56 with .nonactivatingPanel at :36, escape monitor :58-70) plus MCPKeyPanel.swift:10 for the 380 width. The asymmetry with the setup panel is unchanged: MCPSetupPanel (R3-09) overrides close() to clear presentedEntryID and keeps its re-entry guard, while this class has neither.
